description: Pennsylvania-only rules checked against Title 75 and the PennDOT young-driver page. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: The maximum speed 75 Pa.C.S. § 3362 sets for an urban district is 35 mph. That urban limit is in force when
options: The road is inside a city, even with no speed sign
It is posted on official traffic-control devices
It is 35 only during school hours
questions.explanation: Section 3362(a)(1) sets 35 mph in any urban district. Section 3362(b) says a maximum under (a)(1), (a)(1.2), or (a)(3) is not effective unless posted.

questions.q: A 65 or 70 mph freeway limit in Pennsylvania applies
options: On every freeway whether or not a sign is posted
Only on a freeway where the department has posted 65 or 70 mph
Only for passenger cars, never trucks
questions.explanation: Section 3362(a)(1.1) sets 65 or 70 mph for all vehicles on freeways where the department has posted a 65 or 70 mph limit.

questions.q: On a Pennsylvania residence-district highway that is not a numbered traffic route and is classified as a local highway, the statutory maximum is
questions.explanation: Section 3362(a)(1.2) sets 25 mph in that residence district. Like the urban limit, it is not effective until posted.

questions.q: Where 75 Pa.C.S. § 3362 does not set another maximum, the speed limit is
questions.explanation: Section 3362(a)(2) sets 55 mph in other locations. A special hazard can still require a lower speed under section 3361.

questions.q: When passing through a Pennsylvania school zone established under department regulations, the speed limit is
questions.explanation: Section 3365(b) sets 15 mph. An official traffic-control device must mark the beginning and end of the zone, and the department must approve the zone, including its hours.

questions.q: Pennsylvania general impairment under 75 Pa.C.S. § 3802(a)(2) is an alcohol concentration of
options: Any amount for a driver over 21
questions.explanation: The measurement is blood or breath, within two hours after driving. A result of at least 0.10% but less than 0.16% is the high-rate offense in subsection (b). 0.16% or higher is the highest-rate offense in subsection (c).

questions.q: A minor may not drive in Pennsylvania with an alcohol concentration of
options: 0.00 only if the minor is impaired
questions.explanation: Section 3802(e) sets 0.02% or higher in the minor's blood or breath within two hours after driving.

questions.q: The alcohol limit for driving a Pennsylvania commercial vehicle, other than a school bus or school vehicle, is
questions.explanation: Section 3802(f)(1)(i) sets 0.04% or greater for a commercial vehicle other than a school bus or school vehicle. Subsection (f)(1)(ii) sets 0.02% or greater for a school bus or school vehicle.

questions.q: Exceeding a Pennsylvania maximum speed limit by 6 to 10 mph is assessed
questions.explanation: The section 1535 schedule assesses 2 points for 6 to 10 mph over, 3 for 11 to 15, 4 for 16 to 25, and 5 for 26 or more. Driving 31 mph or more over also brings the hearing and sanctions in section 1538(d).

questions.q: Exceeding the special school-zone speed limit in Pennsylvania is assessed
questions.explanation: Section 1535 assesses 3 points for exceeding the section 3365(b) school-zone limit, and a second or subsequent offense also carries a 60-day suspension.

questions.q: Pennsylvania suspends the operating privilege when a driver's record shows
questions.explanation: Section 1539(a) requires suspension at 11 points or more. The first suspension is 5 days for each point. The second is 10 days for each point. The third is 15 days for each point. A later suspension is one year.

questions.q: A driver who was under 18 when the violations were committed, and who accumulates 6 or more Pennsylvania points, receives a first suspension of
questions.explanation: Section 1538(e) also uses that 90-day first suspension when the person is convicted of driving 26 mph or more over the limit for a violation committed before age 18. A subsequent suspension under that subsection is 120 days.

questions.q: For the first six months, a Pennsylvania junior driver may not carry more than one passenger under 18 who is not immediate family unless
options: A parent or guardian rides along
questions.explanation: Section 1503(c)(2.1). After those six months, the limit is three passengers under 18 who are not immediate family, unless a parent or legal guardian is with the driver.

questions.q: PennDOT requires the adult supervising a young driver who holds a learner's permit to be
questions.explanation: PennDOT's young-driver page says an experienced licensed driver aged 21 or older must accompany the permit holder. A junior license also requires six months of learning before the road test.

questions.q: In Pennsylvania, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Pennsylvania issues a learner's permit for a car at 16 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Pennsylvania car permit: 16 years at the earliest.

provenance.manual: Get a Driver's License | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

questions.q: In Pennsylvania, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Pennsylvania requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Pennsylvania complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Pennsylvania requires 65 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a Pennsylvania teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Pennsylvania requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Pennsylvania: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

questions.q: In Pennsylvania, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Pennsylvania, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16½ years.

provenance.manual: Young Driver | Department of Transportation | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Pennsylvania not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Pennsylvania restricts provisional drivers from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: Pennsylvania new drivers: off the road 11 p.m. to 5 a.m..

questions.q: In Pennsylvania, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Pennsylvania drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Pennsylvania car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Pennsylvania car knowledge test has 18 questions.

provenance.manual: Tests | Driver and Vehicle Services | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Pennsylvania car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 83% to pass the Pennsylvania car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Pennsylvania, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Pennsylvania brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: Pennsylvania, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Pennsylvania residential district?
questions.explanation: Pennsylvania sets 25 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Pennsylvania?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Pennsylvania can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Pennsylvania rural interstate: up to 70 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Pennsylvania's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Pennsylvania: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

provenance.manual: Distracted Driving | Department of Transportation | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Pennsylvania?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Pennsylvania, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Pennsylvania left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

questions.q: How is Pennsylvania's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: Pennsylvania seat belt enforcement is secondary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Pennsylvania?
questions.explanation: Pennsylvania requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Pennsylvania: car or booster seat until 8 years.

questions.q: What is Pennsylvania's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Pennsylvania requires at least $15,000 / $30,000 / $5,000.

provenance.manual: Insurance Overview | Driver and Vehicle Services | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
